questions.prompt: You take your rod and you sit by the river for two hours. What is your free time activity?
questions.explanation: A rod and a river go with fishing. Drawing needs a pencil and paper, gardening is the work you do with plants and flowers, and shopping is what you do in the shops.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: "I enjoy ___ a bike in the park after school."
questions.explanation: After the verb enjoy, the activity always takes the -ing form: I enjoy riding a bike. The bare verb "ride", the infinitive "to ride" and the he/she/it form "rides" can never follow enjoy.

questions.prompt: Complete: "This is Amine. ___ kite is red and white."
questions.explanation: The owner is Amine, one boy, so he is "he" and the possessive adjective is His. The word "Her" names a girl, "Its" names a thing or an animal, and "Their" names two people or more.

questions.prompt: Your friend asks: "Why do you enjoy gardening?" Complete your answer: "I enjoy gardening ___ I love flowers."
questions.explanation: The question Why asks for a reason, and the reason is opened by because: I enjoy gardening because I love flowers. The word "and" only joins two ideas, "but" joins two ideas that are different, and "because of" must be followed by a noun, not by a full sentence like I love flowers.

questions.prompt: Salma reads a book every evening of the week. Which sentence says the same thing?

options.text: She always reads in the evening.
She usually reads in the evening.
She sometimes reads in the evening.
She never reads in the evening.

questions.explanation: Every evening means every single time, and the adverb for every time is always. The word "usually" means most times but not all, "sometimes" means not often, and "never" means not one single time.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Amine plays volleyball with his team. His sister ___ volleyball too."
questions.explanation: His sister is one girl, so she is "she", and with he, she or it the verb takes an -s: she plays volleyball. The bare form "play" goes with I, you, we and they, while "playing" and "to play" cannot stand alone as the verb of the sentence.
